A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SIL-C study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, Appendices A-D and checklists support a complete comparison; no material reading gaps were found.

before.justification: v1 reports original robotic simulation experiments on Franka Kitchen and multi-stage Meta-World, including compatibility results, few-shot evaluation, ablations and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains the original robotic simulation results in Sections 5-6 and Appendices C-D, including comparisons reported across four random seeds.

M1.justification: Section 4, Algorithms 1-2 and the pseudocode retain the same prototype memories, skill validation and hooking, training objectives and inference procedure. Changing 'skill-side update' to 'skill space update' is terminological.

E1.justification: Both versions use kitchen-mixed-v0 and the multi-stage Meta-World Easy dataset with the same Emergent/Explicit SIL, few-shot, observation-noise and phase-order scenarios. Added citations in B.1 do not change the represented data or tasks.

E2.justification: The evaluated BUDS/PTGM variants, Skill-prototypes, Instructions, joint-training and multitask controls are retained in their corresponding comparisons. B.3 changes 'three' baseline types to 'four' without adding a comparator.

E3.justification: Both retain four learning phases, 24 task policies per phase, the same preprocessing and model settings, and the same FWT/BWT/AUC evaluation definitions. Figure 4's new axis label does not change reward normalization.

E4.justification: The interface ablations, replay and ordering tests, noise robustness, space-resolution studies, prototype-versus-element retrieval, distance and threshold analyses, and memory/runtime studies are unchanged in Section 6 and Appendices C-D.

E5.justification: B.6 retains four random seeds, mean and standard deviation reporting, and three evaluation repetitions per task. Plot error bars and Table 17's timing mean/variance reporting are also retained.

E6.justification: Numerical tables and findings match, and Figure 4 retains the same bars and error bars despite re-exporting the images. For example, Table 1's SIL-C overall AUC remains 71.8% for Kitchen Emergent and 54.1% for Explicit SIL; appendix results also match.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, Equations (1)-(13), and Appendix D.6 memory/FLOP calculations are unchanged. Neither version contains formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about forward/backward skill compatibility without policy retraining, trajectory-based lazy learning, and efficient, modular skill integration.

C2.justification: The result interpretations and applicability limits are retained, including reliance on simulation with well-defined states, clustering difficulties under more diverse or noisy distributions, and proposed deployment monitoring.

D1.justification: Appendices A-B preserve the implementation details, pseudocode, hyperparameters, hardware, library versions and compute estimates. The code-access statement and link are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds three bibliography entries, references [75]-[77]. B.1 adds citations to the existing Meta-World reference and Shin et al.'s one-shot imitation work. Section 2 and the novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds an Acknowledgement section and makes small terminology and baseline-count edits. B.3 now says 'four' types although it still enumerates only Types I-III. The remaining narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 4 adds a 'Normalized Reward' axis label and adjusts typography and spacing; its plot images are re-exported at lower resolution. Acknowledgements and added references reflow the back matter. Other figures and tables retain their designs.

improvement.justification: The central argument and empirical support are unchanged. Added funding disclosure, benchmark attribution and Figure 4's axis label provide small benefits, while Figure 4 loses sharpness and B.3 introduces a category-count inconsistency. These limited editorial tradeoffs leave overall paper quality effectively unchanged.
